**Visual Analysis:**

- **Affected part**: Whole plant — the tomato plant has completely collapsed and is lying flat on the black plastic mulch
- **Key features**:
  - Total plant wilt and collapse, stems splayed across the ground
  - Left portion of plant is severely desiccated/dead (brown, shriveled leaves)
  - Right portion still shows some green leaves but is visibly wilted and falling over
  - No white fungal mycelium or cottony growth visible (rules out Southern Blight, Sclerotinia)
  - No obvious powdery coatings or leaf spot patterns
  - Collapse appears to originate at or near the stem base/soil line
  - Typical commercial tomato field setting (black plastic mulch)

**Reasoning through classes:**

- **Southern Blight / Sclerotinia**: Both require visible white mycelial mats — none present here
- **Verticillium / Fusarium Wilt**: Would show slower, more gradual one-sided yellowing/V-lesions on leaves, not full collapse
- **Alternaria Stem Canker**: Dark concentric ring cankers at soil line causing girdle and collapse — possible but no visible canker lesions discernible
- **Southern Bacterial Wilt**: Perfectly matches — starts with afternoon wilting, progresses to permanent wilt, brown cankers and root rot at stem base, vascular discoloration, eventual full plant collapse. No fungal structures expected. The complete, rapid collapse of the whole plant lying on the mulch is a hallmark presentation.
- **Bacterial Wilt**: Listed with only "cucurbit yellow vine decline, Fusarium" — insufficient differentiation

The complete, sudden, non-fungal plant collapse at the soil line in a commercial tomato field is the classic presentation of **Southern Bacterial Wilt** (*Ralstonia solanacearum*).
